question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution:
The correct answer is '**fatal**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage discusses the severity and danger of the accident described.
 
• The appropriate adjective should indicate something life-threatening or very serious.
 
• "**Fatal**" fits well as it means causing death, which aligns with the context of describing a severe accident on the road.
 
• Other options ("**wonderful**", "**happening**", "**harmless**") do not fit the context of describing a potentially deadly accident.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

Complete Passage: *It is the mad* *craze__* *for speed that is responsible for many motor accidents. Only last year, I* *__witnessed__* *what might have been a* *__fatal__* *accident on Kashmir Road. I was motoring down* **________***Srinagar; and as I was nearing Kohala, I came upon the* **________***of two cars on the road.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Wonderful (शानदार): "Wonderful" means extremely good, which does not fit the context of a deadly accident.
 
• Happening (भीतर): "Happening" means taking place, which does not align with the idea of describing the severity of an accident.
 
• Harmless (निर्दोष): "Harmless" means not causing harm, which does not fit the description of a serious accident.
